title: Health status and mobility limitations are associated with residential and employment status in schizophrenia and bipolar disorder
cohort_overlap_notes: Suffolk County Mental Health Project 20-year follow-up; same cohort as strassnig2018. The 128 analysed here are a complete-data subset of the 233 analysed in strassnig2018, so the two reports' figures must never be pooled.
notes: Table 1 (p. 182) prints gainful employment as 60 (20.6%) for schizophrenia (n=80) and 23 (53.4%) for bipolar disorder (n=48). Neither count reproduces its own percentage and the counts sum to 83 of 128 (64.8%) against the text's 32.9% employed. No numerator is recoverable without back-calculating from a percentage, so none was recorded. Abstract says the analysis sample was 122; Results say 128.

title: Associations of independent living and labor force participation with impairment indicators in schizophrenia and bipolar disorder at 20-year follow-up
cohort_overlap_notes: Suffolk County Mental Health Project 20-year follow-up; same cohort as strassnig2017 and wholly contains strassnig2017's 128 analysed participants.
notes: Selected report for suffolk_county at 240 months: larger analysis population and counts that reproduce printed percentages exactly. The percentage column of Table 1 is shifted by one row; see conflict_note on the two outcome rows and inconsistencies.md.

title: Frailty affects employment outcomes in patients with schizophrenia in noncompetitive employment: A 4-year longitudinal study
cohort_overlap_notes: Yuli Hospital therapeutic community, Hualien, Taiwan; overlapping sample with wang2020c (561 here against 525 there, same recruitment window and same inclusion criteria). wang2020 is off the screening list (D10.1) and no figure was taken from it.
notes: Employment is reported only as mean cumulative work duration (months per year) and mean cumulative income (USD per year) at 1, 2, 3 and 4 years. No count of employed persons and no employment proportion is printed anywhere, so no numerator or denominator is recoverable. No outcome row extracted.

title: Symptomatic remission affects employment outcomes in schizophrenia patients
cohort_overlap_notes: Yuli Hospital therapeutic community, Hualien, Taiwan; overlapping sample with wang2020b. Neither report cross-references the other and the recruited totals differ (525/550 here against 561 there).
notes: Employment is reported only as mean cumulative on-the-job duration (months per year) and mean income (NT$ per year) at 1 and 2 years. Table 1's initial employment type (workshop 323, sheltered 68, supported 134 = 525) is a baseline allocation to a rehabilitation stream, not an observed employment status at a follow-up timepoint, and the paper prints no employed/not-employed count at either follow-up. No outcome row extracted.

title: Vocational functioning in young people accessing services for first-episode psychosis and ultra-high risk of psychosis: A longitudinal naturalistic cohort study
journal: Australian & New Zealand Journal of Psychiatry
cohort_overlap_notes: Describes two parallel samples from the headspace Early Psychosis programme: headspace_hep_fep_au (FEP, n=1574) and headspace_hep_uhr_au (UHR, n=1515). The provisional single manifest cohort headspace_hep_au is refuted; see manifest_changes.csv. brown2022 is off the screening list (D10.1) and no figure was imported from it.
notes: Results extracted for the FEP cohort only. The UHR cohort is chr and is barred from the primary synthesis outright (SAP section 7); its figures are in the same Table 2 if a CHR analysis is ever added.

title: Factors associated with employment and hospitalizations in early-onset psychosis: a clinical study with register-based follow-up
cohort_overlap_notes: Pools the baseline samples of four Danish clinical studies (EOPC, Attention, DBUP, TEA) with Danish national register follow-up. Thirteen participants were in both Attention and TEA and are counted once. No cohort overlap with any other report in this batch.
notes: paid_any is NOT identified: the register variable classifies supported employment together with unemployment under 'social benefits', so zero paid work is not separable from positive paid work. Bounds 49 <= paid_any <= 155 of 198. Follow-up is a common calendar census date, giving elapsed follow-ups of 4.5 to 23.5 years.
